common_name: Rosy Lights Azalea (Cold-Hardy Fragrant Deciduous Rose-Pink Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; Rosy Lights, part of the University of Minnesota Northern Lights series bred for exceptional cold hardiness, bears fragrant rose-pink flowers.

directions: Plant in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to morning sun. Rosy Lights, part of the University of Minnesota's Northern Lights azalea series bred specifically for extreme cold hardiness, bears clusters of fragrant, rose-pink, funnel-shaped flowers on bare branches in mid-spring before the deciduous foliage fully expands, followed by good yellow-orange fall color. Unlike the evergreen azaleas more common in Southern landscapes, this deciduous type drops its leaves each winter but rewards gardeners at the colder edge of azalea range with reliable, fragrant bloom. Water deeply during dry spells and prune lightly right after flowering, since next year's buds set on the current season's growth.
